cohort: Sixty-three pregnant women with sickle cell disease (SCD) managed at a tertiary hospital in Nigeria between January 1, 2016 and December 31, 2020.
finding: Pregnant women with sickle cell disease (SCD) generally experienced good fetal-maternal outcomes, though lack of antenatal care (ANC) and lower educational attainment were linked to poorer pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: 46.1% of the women in the study had a caesarean delivery.
